oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is an aryloxypropanolamine beta-blocker analog with a tert-butylamino group and a para urea-cyclohexyl substituent; transferable beta-blocker gold contexts report absolute oral bioavailability values of 48-100% (timolol 48-75%, metoprolol 84% in cirrhosis, propranolol 54-79% in cirrhosis), all above the 20% threshold.

L4 solubility and permeability records for beta-blocker analogs show aqueous solubility of at least 1 mg/mL (atenolol, propranolol, acebutolol, and a urea-containing aryloxypropanolamine analog) and propranolol Caco-2 permeability of about 3.4-3.7 x 10^-5 cm/s, supporting adequate intestinal absorption for this chemotype.

L5 gut-wall records show propranolol has high, symmetrical passive permeability with no P-gp/BCRP efflux, and atenolol has modest paracellular permeability; the celiprolol P-gp record indicates intestinal efflux for a close urea-containing beta-blocker analog but provides no F value and does not affirm F < 20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule; prediction relies on transfer from beta-blocker contexts.
No query-specific permeability, solubility, or efflux measurement is available; L4/L5 records are for structurally related analogs.
First-pass metabolism and systemic clearance of the urea-cyclohexyl aryloxypropanolamine are not directly measured.
The celiprolol P-gp efflux record is mechanistic and does not quantify oral bioavailability for the query or for celiprolol itself.
content.decision_summary: L5 gut-wall/intestinal-metabolism records add no affirmative threshold-relevant evidence for F < 20%; propranolol no-efflux records support high passive permeability for the beta-blocker chemotype, and the celiprolol P-gp record is a mechanistic concern for a close analog but not a direct F outcome. Combined with transferable beta-blocker gold F values of 48-100% and favorable solubility/permeability for analogs, the prediction remains high.
